name: Old Jaffa Port
desc: A 4,000-year-old harbor where the stones out-age everyone's opinions. Sunset here costs nothing and fixes most moods.

name: Carmel Market
desc: Vendors yelling, strawberries flying, halva samples if you time it right. The soundtrack of Tel Aviv, free admission.

name: Jaffa Flea Market
desc: Rugs, vinyl and somebody's grandma's chandeliers spilling into the alleys. Treasure-hunt by day, bar-hop the same stalls by night.

name: Rothschild Boulevard
desc: Bauhaus buildings, coffee kiosks and scooters dodging dogs. The city's living room — stroll it like you already pay rent here.

name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
desc: Angular concrete outside, Israeli masters and big moderns inside. Cool air and cooler art when the beach gets loud.

name: Hilton Beach
desc: Surfers, the crack of matkot paddles, and a dog beach next door. Salt water is free and so is the vitamin D.

name: Park HaYarkon
desc: Tel Aviv's green lung — rowboats, endless lawns, parrots heckling from the trees. Naps here count as sightseeing.

name: White City Bauhaus District
desc: A UNESCO stash of 4,000 Bauhaus buildings going golden at dusk. Architecture nerd-out with a zero-dollar entry fee.

name: Namal Tel Aviv (Old Port)
desc: A boardwalk built in wooden waves, sea spray included. Broke-friendly hangout engineering at its finest.
